messages:
sre-bot: Incident 1771023456 - HIGH: Autoscale pool us-west-2 experiencing repeated throttle events and queue depth spikes (tokens/sec burst). Pagering on-call

alex: seeing it too — from dashboards: queue_depth per worker went from ~10 -> 120 within 30s, tokens/sec spiked 4x. Throttles increased and we hit reserve burst limits.

mira: confirmed customer-visible errors? any 5xx or rate-limited client reports?

ryan: SLO page shows a small blip in completion failures for generation endpoints (~0.6% -> 3.2%) starting 14:21 UTC. No broad 5xx cascades yet, but tail latency exploded.

jess: @alex can you open a mitigation runbook? I want to coordinate handoff if we need >15m action.

alex: opening runbook now. Quick mitigation: 1) scale up dedicated pool by 20% (add 2 nodes), 2) enable fallback routing to smaller model variant for non-critical routes, 3) apply token-rate soft cap on noisy client. I'll trigger (1) and (2).

alex: /deploy-scale --pool us-west-2 --add 2 -> triggering autoscale-up job (job id: scale-17710235). ETA ~90s.

sre-bot: scale job scale-17710235 started by alex — estimated ready 90s.

mira: while scaling, can we temporarily mute the queue_depth alert to avoid repeated pages? It's noisy and obscuring real events. We should suppress on-call paging for 5m during the incident mitigation.

ryan: +1. Current queue_depth alert uses raw per-worker instantaneous value > 80 for 1m. That fires a lot during short bursts. We should mute pages and rely on aggregate tokens/sec > threshold for sustained load.

jess: Agree. Mute paging for queue_depth (rule id: qd-serve-01) for 5m and add a note. We'll still post in channel.

alex: muted qd-serve-01 for 5m. Also enabling fallback routing now: route non-privileged routes to model-small-1 when latency > 1.2s.

sre-bot: scale job scale-17710235 finished — 2 nodes added, pool capacity increased.

mira: pool capacity increase visible. Throttles dropping. Tail latency improving but still noisy.

ryan: I pushed a temporary throttle rule: per-client token/sec soft-limit 8000 with 10s cooldown. That should slow an aggressive test client.

product-ops: FYI we identified a partner running an unbounded load test against generation APIs around 14:20 UTC. We contacted them to pause. They said it was an automated health check gone rogue.

alex: thanks. With partner paused and nodes up, errors dropping to baseline. We should still follow up on alerting though — this will repeat if another burst hits.

jess: Post-incident actions proposed (short list):
- Replace instantaneous per-worker queue_depth pages with 1m and 5m moving-average aggregation for paging. (owner: ryan)
- Create a composite alert: sustained tokens/sec per-pool > X for >2m AND throttle_rate > Y triggers page. (owner: mira)
- Add suppressed alert window when autoscale job is running to avoid noise during expected capacity changes. (owner: alex)
- Dashboard: new panel 'pool-surge-overview' showing tokens/sec, queue_depth MA(1m/5m), throttle_events, and top clients by tokens/sec. (owner: jess)
